minutes.headline: Back-lot cemetery expansion cost estimate came in far above the $50,000 budgeted, forcing redesign before bidding.
minutes.summary: The Cemetery Commission approved routine minutes, Memorial Day flowers, a $20,000 transfer from sale-of-lots funds, a Fish Street plaque design, and a lot exchange recognizing a donor family. Most of the meeting was spent on the DPW director's report that the engineering estimate for the South Cemetery back-lot expansion came back far higher than the $50,000 placeholder budgeted, prompting discussion of cost-cutting (reusing town millings, cheaper gravel, dropping engineering-during-construction costs) and funding options (sale-of-lots balance, rate increases, possible non-resident burials) before the project can go out to bid.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of Friday, December 19th and February 26th together
Purchase flowers for the front of both north and south cemeteries for Memorial Day
Notify the town they want to transfer $20,000 from sale of lots for cemetery care/improvement/expansion
Approve the plaque design for the Fish Street Cemetery
Accept the donated lot from the Watson family and exchange designation of 29UC/5U so the commission can resell the freed cremation lot

budget_items.what_was_said: The commission listed already-committed costs: gravestone straightening and repair, the Fish Street Cemetery wall, and plaque/stonework.
Members recalled last year's flower cost and discussed capping this year's purchase, unsure of exact prior figure amid inflation.

The commission discussed whether a $20,000 warrant article was still needed for town meeting, and learned the town manager said it was not required going forward; a written authorization to the treasurer suffices instead.

budget_items.topic: South Cemetery / Fish Street project funding need
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reviewed the outstanding commitment for South Cemetery and Fish Street work against the current balance to determine how much more was needed before the $20,000 transfer.

budget_items.topic: Remaining balance after transfer and flowers
budget_items.what_was_said: After applying the planned $20,000 transfer and assumed $600 flower cost, the commission worked out roughly how much would remain for the rest of the year.

The DPW director presented a new engineering cost estimate for the back-lot cemetery expansion that came in far above the original placeholder figure, calling it a shock, and outlined ways to bring it down.
The director proposed eliminating this line since he could answer bidder questions himself, paying an engineer hourly only if needed.
A line for moving contractor equipment onto site was discussed as an area that might be trimmed or folded into unit prices.

budget_items.topic: Sale of lots and perpetual care account balances
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed the sale-of-lots balance after the planned transfer and a separate, larger perpetual care account whose interest only can be used.
It was suggested that allowing non-residents to be buried in the cemetery, as some other towns do, could bring in additional revenue toward the expansion.
A per-stump estimate was called unrealistically low given hauling and documentation requirements, with a revised total suggested to be much higher.
The department is rehiring two part-time seasonal helpers from last year, within a limited budget that must last through the end of the fiscal year.

transfers.description: $20,000 from the sale-of-lots account to fund cemetery care, improvement and expansion

decisions.decision: Going forward, the commission will submit written authorization to the town treasurer/accountant to transfer sale-of-lots funds rather than seeking a town meeting warrant article each year.
The commission agreed it does not want to drain the sale-of-lots account to a low balance and will revise the expansion cost estimate before deciding how much of the project to bid.
The commission cannot solicit donations from town residents directly since it is a town body, though it could accept unsolicited gifts or support a resident-formed 501(c)3.
The commission will not go out to bid until the funding amount is confirmed; the DPW director will first revise the cost estimate and reduce scope where possible.
Board members will take home the revised cemetery rules and regulations document to review before discussing changes at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: An engineering estimate for the South Cemetery back-lot expansion came back far above the amount budgeted, so the commission held off on bidding and asked the DPW director to cut scope and revise it.
The commission voted to transfer a sum from the sale-of-lots account toward cemetery care and the expansion, but agreed not to draw that account down too far.
Going forward the commission will authorize sale-of-lots transfers in writing to the town treasurer instead of seeking a town meeting warrant article each year.
Members discussed funding options for the expansion, including a rate increase and allowing non-resident burials, which the town does not currently permit.
The commission accepted a donated lot from the Watson family and approved a lot-designation exchange so the freed cremation lot can be resold.

why_it_matters: A cemetery expansion project residents may have assumed was funded at its original estimate now needs redesign or more money before it can go out to bid.
How the commission pays for it -- sale-of-lots funds, a rate increase, or opening burials to non-residents -- affects what future lot buyers and taxpayers are asked to cover.
The shift to written treasurer authorization for these transfers means this kind of spending will no longer come before town meeting as a warrant article.
